doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Rehearsals and ever-changing parts
summary: Players sang, memorised and noted parts in dots and dashes; parts changed daily and with each added player, so missing a rehearsal left you lost.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Would Sun Ra vocalize things like no don’t make it sound like that, make it sound like this, and then would he sing at you?
He’d have you either sing it, play it and memorize it, and then change it. After you remember your parts he’d give you another one.
I can picture myself and trying to deal with that and I’d like have a little, some score paper and I’d be trying to write it down.

Yes that’s what we were doing on the side of the music we’d put the little changes on the side and we’d look at the music — it was little dots and dashes so that we could remember how to phrase something.
Yeah, and then the next day it’s something different.

And then that’s gone. You’d get something new. If you’d come to rehearsal today and you got your part and you played it perfect, good or whatever. You come tomorrow and you didn’t come near, then when you come the next day the music changed. Your part don’t fit no more. You have to get your new part, if you miss a rehearsal. So in other words every time there was a rehearsal you’d have to be there.
And eventually there’s a performance or a concert and there, maybe by Sun Ra’s design this music is going to be changed that day also?

Right. Because he got somebody else added in. Every person added in the music changed. So he’d either get some musicians and add them in, and it would change. So then what you did with the other musicians don’t fit with these. You see? And that’s frustrating because we all, when you learn your parts you walk in and sit down in your chair and you’re ready to roll. And you get there and the song don’t go that way no more. Because you wasn’t at rehearsal yesterday to get the change. And then the change is added then you’re lost. You’re trying to play it the old way and the leader changed the expression.
